title: Lawrence Lemieux Leaves the Race
text:
At the 1988 Seoul Olympics, the sailing events were held off the port of Busan, South Korea. On September 24 a strong wind whipped up the sea. Lawrence Lemieux of Canada, sailing alone in the Finn class, was running second in his race and had a real chance at a medal.

On a nearby course, a two-man boat from Singapore in the 470 class had capsized in the rough water. One sailor, Joseph Chan, was injured and had been swept away from the boat, and his crewmate Siew Shaw Her was clinging to the hull. Rescue boats were busy with other boats in trouble.

Lemieux changed course. He sailed to the men, pulled the injured Chan out of the water, kept both men with him, and waited until a patrol boat arrived to take them. Then he went back to the race and finished well down the fleet.

The race jury, recognizing what he had done, gave him back the position he had held before the rescue. He finished eleventh overall. At a ceremony in Seoul, IOC President Juan Antonio Samaranch honored him with the Pierre de Coubertin Medal for sportsmanship.
lesson: When someone near you is in danger, your own goals can wait. No prize is worth more than helping a person who needs you right now.
people: Lawrence Lemieux, Joseph Chan, Siew Shaw Her
source: Official Report of the Games of the XXIVth Olympiad, Seoul 1988; contemporary press reports
